turn.userText: What does the heating element do?

response.text: It turns electricity into heat to warm the water.

turn.userText: Why does a full kettle take longer to boil?

response.text: A full kettle has more water to warm up. It needs more energy, so it takes longer to boil.

turn.userText: Why does a higher-power kettle boil faster?

response.text: The element turns electricity into heat. A higher-power one gives more heat each second, so the water boils sooner.

turn.userText: How does the heat spread through the water?

response.text: Warm water rises and cool water sinks. These loops carry the heat all through the water.

turn.userText: What makes the kettle switch itself off?

response.text: Steam from the boiling water heats a little strip inside. The strip bends and clicks the kettle off.

turn.userText: Why does limescale make my kettle slower?

response.text: The element makes heat that warms the water. Limescale coats it like a crust that blocks the heat, so boiling takes longer.

turn.userText: What shape is the lens?

response.text: It is a convex lens, thicker in the middle than at the edges.

turn.userText: Why does light bend in the glass?

response.text: Light moves slower in glass than in air. That change in speed makes it turn a little as it goes in.

turn.userText: Why do letters look bigger through it?

response.text: A magnifying glass is thicker in the middle than at the edges. Light bends as it passes from air into glass and back out. Held close, it makes an enlarged, upright image of the letters.

turn.userText: Why is the picture upside down when I hold it far away?

response.text: When you hold the glass far away, it shows the picture upside down.

turn.userText: How can it burn a leaf in the sun?

response.text: It squeezes bright sunlight into a tiny spot. That spot gets very hot and can burn the leaf.

turn.userText: Is a magnifying glass thicker in the middle?

response.text: Yes, it is. A magnifying glass is thicker in the middle than at the edges.

turn.userText: How does a string make sound?

response.text: The string moves back and forth after you pluck it. It pushes on the air, which makes sound waves.

turn.userText: Why does tightening the string change the note?

response.text: Tightening the string makes it move back and forth faster. That faster shaking pushes the air to make a higher note.

turn.userText: What happens when I press a fret?

response.text: You make the part that shakes shorter. That shorter shake makes a higher note.

turn.userText: Why do the thick strings sound low?

response.text: Thick strings are heavier so they move back and forth more slowly. That slow move makes a low sound.

turn.userText: Why is the guitar hollow?

response.text: The hollow body shakes along with the strings. That makes the sound louder.

turn.userText: Does a tighter string vibrate faster?

response.text: Yes, it does. A tighter string vibrates faster, so its note sounds higher.

turn.userText: Does water boil at a lower temperature on a mountain?

response.text: Yes, it does. Up high the air pushes down less, so bubbles can form cooler. The hot water is a little less hot than at home.

turn.userText: Why does a microwave heat water differently?

response.text: A microwave sends tiny waves right into the drink. They make the water bits shake all through at once. Imagine heat starting everywhere, not just rising up from below.

turn.userText: Who invented the electric kettle?

response.text: Early electric kettles were made in the 1890s by lighting companies. Later inventors added the switch that turns the kettle off by itself.

turn.userText: Is it cheaper to boil only the water I need?

response.text: Yes. Less water needs less energy to get hot. So the element uses less electricity.

turn.userText: How do glasses help people see?

response.text: Glasses bend light before it goes into your eye. That helps your eye focus it in the right spot so things look clear.

turn.userText: Do telescopes use lenses too?

response.text: Yes. Many telescopes use lenses to bend light and make far things look bigger. Some use curved mirrors instead to do the same job.

turn.userText: Why do my eyes have a lens?

response.text: Your eye has a small lens to bend light onto the back of your eye. That helps make a clear picture for you to see.

turn.userText: What is a concave lens?

response.text: A concave lens is thin in the middle and thicker at the edges. It spreads light out and makes things look smaller.

turn.userText: How does a piano make its sound?

response.text: Inside a piano, little hammers hit strings when you press a key. The hit strings shake and push the air to make sound. Short, tight strings sound high and long, loose ones sound low.

turn.userText: Why does a violin sound different from a guitar?

response.text: A violin is smaller with shorter, tighter strings, so it sings higher than a guitar. It is played with a bow that keeps the string buzzing, and its small box shapes the tone.

turn.userText: How do electric guitars work without a hollow body?

response.text: Electric guitars use small magnets called pickups to feel the metal string shake. The pickups turn that shake into a tiny electric signal. A speaker amp then makes that signal big and loud.

turn.userText: What is an octave?

response.text: An octave is a jump from one note to the same note higher or lower. The higher note vibrates twice as fast but still sounds like family.

turn.userText: ¿Por qué tarda más en hervir una tetera llena?

response.text: El elemento convierte la electricidad en calor. Si pones más agua, necesitas más energía. Por eso tú esperas más con la tetera llena.

turn.userText: ¿Qué hace que la tetera se apague sola?

response.text: El vapor calienta una tira metálica dentro de la tetera. La tira se dobla con el calor y la apaga por ti.

turn.userText: ¿Por qué se ven más grandes las letras?

response.text: Tu lupa es más gruesa en el centro. La luz se dobla al pasar por el vidrio. Así ves las letras más grandes y derechas.

turn.userText: ¿Por qué cambia la nota al tensar la cuerda?

response.text: Si la aprietas, la cuerda vibra más rápido. Por eso la nota suena más aguda.

turn.userText: ¿Cómo funcionan las gafas?

response.text: Algunas gafas usan lentes que doblan la luz para que veas más claro. Imagina cómo cambian las letras de un cuento cuando miras con ellas.

turn.userText: ¿Cómo suena un piano?

response.text: El piano suena con cuerdas que vibran dentro de él. Tú puedes notar sonidos graves y agudos, igual que en una guitarra.
